title: Many honors lawful toward the living are not lawful toward the spirits of the dead
source_text: XXX. Praeterea Scholae Reformatae Doctores non solum censent illicitum esse, quae ad cultum divinum pertinent, ad Angelos, vel Sanctos in caelum receptos transferre, sed etiam multae sunt cultus & honoris species, quibus erga homines nobiscum in terra viventes uti licet, quas tamen, eorundem doctorum judicio, ratio & pietas vetat erga mortuorum spiritus adhibere.
pass_a_gloss: Besides, the doctors of the Reformed School not only judge it unlawful to transfer to angels, or to Saints received into heaven, the things that belong to the divine cult, but there are also many species of cult and honor which it is lawful to use toward men living with us on earth, which nevertheless, in the judgment of those same doctors, reason and piety forbid to be applied to the spirits of the dead.
pass_b_english: It is not only divine worship that may not be moved over to angels or Saints in heaven.
Many honors that are lawful toward people living with us on earth are, by reason and piety, forbidden toward the spirits of the dead.

choices.why: The ban is wider than latria; it includes civil signs that require presence.
